title: What acceleration means: speeding up and slowing down

forces.label: Engine force
forces.ask: What makes a car speed up?

explain.say: Think of a car pulling away from traffic lights in Cairo. You get pressed back into your seat. That feeling is acceleration, which means your velocity is changing. Let us look at the forces that cause it.

draw.text: What acceleration means: speeding up and slowing down

forces.label: Engine force
forces.ask: What makes a car speed up?

explain.say: See the big arrow pointing forward? That is the engine force, pushing the car along. It is bigger than the arrow pointing back. Unequal forces are called unbalanced, and they make the car speed up. Which arrow is longer?

forces.label: Engine force
forces.ask: What makes a car speed up?

explain.say: The forward one, yes! The small arrow pointing back is air resistance, the air pushing against the car. The difference between the two arrows makes the car accelerate. Acceleration is how much the speed changes each second.

forces.label: Engine force
forces.ask: What makes a car speed up?

explain.say: Now the driver brakes. Look, the big arrow points backwards now: brake friction. The car still moves forward, but the force points back, so it slows down. Slowing down is also acceleration, often called deceleration. Which way does the overall force point now?

forces.label: Brake friction
forces.ask: What makes a car slow down?

explain.say: Backwards, well spotted! So remember: an unbalanced force changes velocity, making it faster, slower or turning it. Wow fact: a fighter pilot in a tight turn can feel nine times their own weight. Next time you ride in a car, notice which way you are pushed.

forces.label: Brake friction
forces.ask: What makes a car slow down?

faq.q: What makes a car speed up?
faq.a: An unbalanced forward force. When the engine push is bigger than air resistance and friction, the car accelerates.
Air resistance is the push of air against something moving through it. It grows bigger the faster you go.

faq.q: What makes a car slow down?
faq.a: A force pointing backwards, like brake friction or air resistance, that is bigger than any forward push. It makes the velocity smaller.
Acceleration equals change in velocity divided by time. Going from 0 to 10 metres per second in 5 seconds is 2 metres per second squared.
Yes. Velocity includes direction, so changing direction, even at a steady speed, is acceleration.
asks: Can you accelerate without speeding up?

facts: Acceleration is measured in metres per second squared (m/s²).
Near Earth, a falling object accelerates at about 9.8 m/s² when air resistance is small.

quiz.say: A bike speeds up from 2 m/s to 8 m/s in 3 s. What is its acceleration?
quiz.show: A bike speeds up from 2 m/s to 8 m/s in 3 s. What is its acceleration?
quiz.why: Change in velocity is 6 m/s, and 6 ÷ 3 = 2 metres per second squared.

wrong.0: Six is the change in velocity; you still divide by the 3 seconds.
wrong.2: That divides 10 by 3; use the change, 8 minus 2.

quiz.say: A car moves forward while the overall force on it points backwards. What happens?
quiz.show: A car moves forward while the overall force on it points backwards. What happens?
quiz.why: A backward resultant force makes the forward velocity smaller: deceleration.

wrong.0: Speeding up needs the overall force pointing the way it moves.
wrong.1: The force slows it gradually; it does not stop in an instant.
